registry.title: Executive summary
registry.description: Three-sentence synthesis of the other selected sections. Always last to generate because it reads their outputs.

registry.title: Usage and volume
registry.description: Session evaluation volume and cart value against the previous quarter, split by shopper segment. The baseline "are they using it more" question.

registry.title: Feature adoption
registry.description: Which engine capabilities the account fires, which are newly adopted or lapsing, and which are covered by their plan but never used. Use when the conversation is about depth of use or expansion headroom.

registry.title: Campaign performance
registry.description: Per-campaign redemptions, redemption rate and discount value with a quarter-over-quarter comparison, sliced by shopper segment. Use when the customer wants to know which promotions worked.

registry.title: Loyalty health
registry.description: Points issued against points burned, and the resulting outstanding liability. Only relevant to accounts running a loyalty programme.

registry.title: Integration health
registry.description: API error rates and latency by application. Use when there were incidents worth pre-empting, or when the account has raised reliability concerns.

registry.title: Worth discussing
registry.description: The handful of movements that are both statistically unusual and commercially material, ranked. Use in almost every QBR; this is the section that makes the review feel prepared rather than reported.

registry.title: Since we last spoke
registry.description: What was agreed at the last review and where each action stands, plus the calls and notes bearing on this quarter. The only section with no query against the warehouse. Use in any QBR that follows a previous one.

registry.title: Expansion signals
registry.description: Paid features the account is entitled to but does not use, and capabilities whose usage is growing fast enough to justify a bigger plan. Use when the CSM is preparing a commercial conversation.

must_cover: Any feature in a newly_adopted or growing state, named, with its volume
Any feature that is entitled but never used, which is an expansion opening
Any feature that has lapsed or is declining
must_not: Describing a feature as unavailable when is_entitled is true
Any figure that does not appear in the payload
Inventing a reason for adoption or non-adoption
writing_rules.tone: A CSM presenting to their customer. Concrete about what changed. Frame unused entitlements as available capability, not as a failure.

must_cover: The single largest quarter-over-quarter mover, named, with both values
Whether that movement concentrates in one shopper segment, using the breakdown
One forward-looking hook the CSM can open a conversation with
must_not: Speculating about causes that are not present in the data
Any figure that does not appear in the payload
Recommending a specific discount level or commercial term
writing_rules.tone: A CSM presenting to their customer. Factual and specific. No hype, no apology, no filler. Name campaigns by name.

must_cover: Each ranked movement, named, with its observed value and its baseline
Why it is worth raising, in business terms rather than statistical ones
What the CSM should ask or say about it
must_not: Mentioning z-scores or standard deviations to the customer
Any movement not present in the ranked payload
Any figure that does not appear in the payload
Asserting a cause the data does not establish
writing_rules.tone: A CSM who has done their homework. Lead with what it means for the customer, not with how it was detected. Direct, no alarm.

evidence.title: Quarterly check-in, Acme Commerce
evidence.snippet: "We cut the winback audience down to ninety days in the first week of April, and honestly we expected the redemption rate to drop. That was the trade."

context_rules: Context explains a movement. It is never the source of a figure.
Cite evidence by its citation_id in square brackets, for example [C1].
Quote only what a snippet says, character for character. Paraphrase otherwise.
Do not cite a citation_id that is not in this payload.

must_cover: Every action agreed at the previous review, with its current status
Who owns each one that is still open
must_not: Any figure or date; this section is qualitative, and figures belong in the sections that queried the warehouse for them
Any commitment not present in the payload
Characterising an open action as a failure on the customer's part
writing_rules.tone: A CSM picking up a conversation, not auditing one. Brief. State what was agreed and where it stands.
